scope: Local macOS arm64 private direct-Chrome A/B/B/A diagnostic. No Connect gateway, installed qualification, provider operation or production policy change.
status: completed diagnostic; all four original media verdicts remain failed
question: Does removing the production SDK encoded-transform and periodic-keyframe path restore encoding cadence and coded AV under the same impairment profile?
answer: No consistent improvement was observed. Sparse encoding and coded-AV failure occurred in both no-transform repeats as well as both production repeats.

controls.capture: Same generated coded-content source,640×360/30fps capture constraints; actual capture medians29–30fps.
controls.sender: Identical VP8 primary with matching RTX, maintain-resolution, maximum1,000,000bps and30fps. Codec/capture/sender/transform controls checked throughout diagnostics and at boundaries.
controls.receiver: Same decoded audio/video marker observers and unchanged qualification predicates. Local sender index feeds the opposite receiver index.
controls.network: Owned loopback Chrome UDP target and both selected remote proxy paths verified through every observation window; no external ICE.
controls.intervention: Production installs the existing SDK worker and periodic keyframe adapter. None retains exact VP8/RTX preferences but installs neither. Existing worker requirement remains failed in the none arm.

interpretation_limits: Removing worker and periodic requests together is a bundled intervention. These trials establish that the sparse symptom can occur without that path or the Connect gateway; they do not establish equivalence, exclude a transform performance contribution, or identify a particular controller defect.
Same seed is not identical packet realization when the sender emits different traffic. Two repeats per arm are a bounded diagnostic, not a statistical equivalence proof.

No-transform senders produced zero in-window keyframes; initial pre-window keyframes are outside this count. Production produced55–60. The intervention operated but did not restore sustained capture-rate encoding or coded AV.
Proxy final snapshots leave up to one unaccounted in-flight packet per direction in some cases; there is no exact final packet-accounting claim.
Retained packet_send_delay_seconds is cumulative, not per-packet queue latency. Chrome target/available bitrate fields are not raw delay/loss controller reconstruction.
The production worker and required keyframe interval of at most one second remain mandatory. This diagnostic does not authorize their removal or any weaker cadence, impairment, or AV thresholds.
